title: GPU — Where It Stands
thesis: An in-house wgpu plane that does what neither three.js (render-only) nor taichi (compute-only) does: compute and render on one device, zero-copy. Its distinctive core is a self-tuning foundry; real consumers are accelerated and verified (t-SNE 5-8x, UMAP up to 16x, k-means 6x, neural forward 5x, exact vector search 18x), always with a bit-identical CPU fallback. What it refuses by measured decision — f64 on GPU, multi-GPU, deep 3D — are scope boundaries, not oversights.

lanes.note: A checker runs reference vs candidate at a visible and a hidden shape, refusing by name any time under a measured roofline; a shape-keyed store keeps the winner
gpu.zig over vendored wgpu-native v29: generation-keyed handles, bounded VRAM cache, WGSL compile-cache, TDR-safe tiling, async dispatch, live instruments
A WGSL kernel library: matmul (tiled + register-blocked), pairdist, softmax, reductions, FFT convolution (Stockham radix-2), fused multi-head attention
Compute and render in one DLL sharing one device: instanced 2D display list, HarfBuzz text, texture atlas, 3D meshes in one instanced draw; zero-copy proven
t-SNE 5-8x, UMAP 9.8-16.5x, k-means up to 6.1x, semantic index 2-2.5x, neural backbone 5.3x, vector search 17.9x; each with a bit-identical CPU fallback
gpu_wgsl.zig turns a stzKernelMaker spec into elementwise WGSL: f32-only, 20-function whitelist, refuses unknown functions by name; elementwise-only
The transpiler compiles into stz.wasm; same spec -> byte-identical WGSL native vs browser -> f32-exact results (5/5); elementwise kernels only
Upload once -> run N kernels -> read once; every op takes and returns stzGpuBuffer handles; bounded FIFO VRAM cache; single-device, not usage-aware
stz_gpu_wake(cap_ms) does adaptive copies until one runs at full speed; every guard wakes the device before timing; idle-aware routing (GK1b) not built
f32 throughout; f64 refused by measured decision (consumer NVIDIA runs it at 1/64 of f32); the f64 solver tier stays CPU SIMD
Adapter enumeration and selection of one device, per-adapter calibration; no two-device parallelism, out of scope with a pre-written 1.5x kill line
A camera, one directional light, instanced meshes in a single call; no PBR materials, shadows, post-processing or a deep scene graph

standouts: a self-tuning, self-checking calibration foundry: category-of-one
compute and render zero-copy on one device
every GPU route measured, verified, and reversible to CPU
gaps: broaden the kernel transpiler beyond elementwise
